My previous rule wrongly allowed partial matches mixing noise and marker cells (e.g., demo 2's anchor near the original shape was *not* stamped). Strict all-noise matching explains both demos fully. In the test (bg=9, noise=0, marker=5), the shape occurs once at rows 2-6, cols 2-4.

```python
def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter
    cnt = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    bg = cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    markers = [v for v in cnt if v not in (bg, 0)]
    if not markers:
        return [r[:] for r in grid]
    marker = markers[0]
    R, C = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    cells = [(i, j) for i in range(R) for j in range(C) if grid[i][j] == marker]
    r0 = min(i for i, j in cells)
    c0 = min(j for i, j in cells)
    tpl = [(i - r0, j - c0) for i, j in cells]
    H = max(i for i, j in tpl) + 1
    W = max(j for i, j in tpl) + 1
    out = [r[:] for r in grid]
    for a in range(R - H + 1):
        for b in range(C - W + 1):
            if all(grid[a + i][b + j] == 0 for i, j in tpl):
                for i, j in tpl:
                    out[a + i][b + j] = marker
    return out
```

```python
    r0 = min(i for i, j in cells)
    c0 = min(j for i, j in cells)
    tpl = [(i - r0, j - c0) for i, j in cells]
    H = max(i for i, j in tpl) + 1
    W = max(j for i, j in tpl) + 1
    out = [r[:] for r in grid]
    for a in range(R - H + 1):
        for b in range(C - W + 1):
            if all(grid[a + i][b + j] == noise for i, j in tpl):
                for i, j in tpl:
                    out[a + i][b + j] = marker
```
